title: Why revealing the reset word destroys a marginal randomized reset
statement: A half-identity/half-swap mixture erases a binary input in the nonselective state marginal, but the joint pair (chosen word, future state test) still reveals the input. A continuation that sees the key requires a different conditional-reset contract.

requires: continuation observes the chosen control word or its timing leak
provides: counterexample to marginal-reset implies record-visible reset
assumptions: same input bit used in both compared worlds
word is part of the continuation's accessible output
costs: controller privacy, fresh randomness and physical record disposal cannot be assumed free
contract.units: joint-record total variation versus marginal total variation
contract.obstruction: Prevents an incompatible transfer from hidden-key preparation to exposed-record experiments.

evidence.quote: Retaining the sampled word can invalidate the conclusion completely

review.scope: Exact source-supported extraction only; any scoped substantive acceptance is a separate version-bound review overlay.
